title: A derivative-free approach to optimal control problems with piecewise constant Mayer cost function
contribution: Proposes a hybrid method for discretized optimal control with a piecewise constant (floor-type) Mayer cost: NOMAD/Mads with progressive barrier optimizes only the few state variables that affect the discontinuity, while Ipopt solves the smooth trajectory subproblems between them; on four control problems the hybrid finds far lower Bolza costs than Ipopt-only or NOMAD-only approaches.
problem_entry: Application-driven class (precision sports, parking) where PMP is unlikely (optima end on plateau boundaries), smoothing leaves near-zero gradients, and MADS cannot handle the full discretization's size (pp. 2-3).
key_idea: Reformulate min_x as min_y inf_z with y = singular variables (states at indices Λ ⊇ Ω ∪ {N}) given to DFO and z to a smooth inner solver; evaluate the blackbox by a two-phase solve returning (minimal infeasibility, objective) to the progressive barrier instead of +∞ (pp. 3-10).
assumptions: Smooth dynamics, constraints and Lagrange cost; singularities only through a known subset of states; RK4 discretization; h_c(y,·) attains its minimum (Prop. 2.9); all methods run on a smoothed floor (τ = 75) for fair comparison (pp. 4-11).
proof_devices: reformulation equivalence min_x = min_y inf_z with FWD (feasible-well-defined) conditions (Prop. 2.4, p. 6)
one 2-D counterexample per hypothesis of the reformulation (Examples 2.5-2.8, p. 7)
two-phase evaluation: minimize squared violation, then objective under the found violation level (§2.3, pp. 7-8)
experiments: Harmonic oscillator, two Zermelo problems, Lotka-Volterra (N = 400-600), common uncontrolled start and smoothing, MSO vs MDFBBO vs hybrids M{N}, M{N/2,N} by final Bolza cost from legends (e.g. Z1: 32.20, 34.35 vs 4.88, p. 14); single runs, no counts or timings; M{N} failure on LV diagnosed by an infeasibility map (Fig. 9, pp. 16-17).
positioning: Sits between optimal-control direct/indirect methods (PMP for Lipschitz and hybrid systems cited) and DFO (MADS, progressive barrier); distinguishes itself from trajectory-optimization decomposition (needs derivatives) and bilevel optimization (no leader-follower conflict) (pp. 2-5).
writing: Predicts why each naive baseline fails in §1 and §3.2 and checks it in §4 (pp. 3, 10); motivates with everyday examples (darts, parking, p. 2-3); presents the unexpected LV failure as 'intriguing' and analyses it (p. 16).
limits_future: Best Λ is not the smallest; inner Ipopt failures act as code-induced hidden constraints; class of suitable problems unidentified; future: Λ as DFO variables, penalty-relaxed state matching, early-stopped SO surrogates (pp. 15-18).

method_links.note: Division of labour by variable block (DFO outer on singular states, smooth solver inner), not by Search/Poll step; 'each solver to a problem it is designed for'.
Infeasible inner problems return quantified violation plus finite objective to the progressive barrier rather than +∞; inner-solver failures named as hidden constraints.
Small-scale: each hypothesis of the reformulation proposition bounded by a 2-D counterexample; no convergence analysis of the algorithm.
Equal initialization and equal smoothing for fairness, but single runs, final values only, no evaluation budget accounting.
NOMAD's 'critical value of 50' variables motivates giving it only n or 2n state variables.

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: DFO only on the variables carrying the discontinuity, gradient-based inner solver on the rest; possible precursor of the 2026 partitioned structure-aware framework (inference).
Infeasibility of Ipopt's answer plotted over x_N explains why NOMAD stays in a ribbon around the start.

transferable: Return (minimal infeasibility, objective under it) from an infeasible inner optimization to a progressive barrier instead of +∞ (pp. 7-8).
State the failure mechanism of each naive baseline before running it, then check it (pp. 3, 10).
Pair a reformulation proposition with one minimal 2-D counterexample per hypothesis (pp. 6-7).

quotes.text: The main idea is thus to optimize the final state alone via a DFBBO algorithm, while a smooth subproblem, which consists in solving the initial problem with the final state being fixed and with a minimal Lagrange cost, is solved via a SO algorithm.
We could set the value +∞, but such a choice would not provide any information to pursue efficiently the numerical resolution of (R).

title: Quantifying uncertainty with ensembles of surrogates for blackbox optimization
contribution: Turns an ensemble of deterministic surrogates into a pseudo-stochastic model by measuring pairwise trend or feasibility disagreement between members (smooth and nonsmooth versions, objective and constraint versions), and uses it with Bayesian-style subproblems in the MADS Search; better than no-search and quad-search MADS on 3 of 4 expensive problems and much cheaper than kriging.
problem_entry: Ensembles and stochastic models are 'fundamentally separated': ensembles give no uncertainty for Bayesian acquisition, GPs become costly as samples grow (pp. 2-3).
key_idea: Uncertainty = weighted average over model pairs of disagreement in trends (1-cos of simplex gradients, or xor of predicted decrease over a positive spanning set) or in feasibility (sigmoid of product, xor of signs), scaled by 10·Var of cached values; P, PI, EI replaced by sigmoid-based substitutes; solved in the MADS Search and projected on the mesh (pp. 8-16).
assumptions: Bounds unrelaxable, c_j relaxable; no probabilistic foundation claimed; independence of constraints in P(x); many constants set by preliminary tests (factor 10, N_best, λ, simplex 0.001, PSS 0.005) (pp. 2, 11-15, 35).
proof_devices: convergence inherited from MADS because every Search candidate is projected onto the mesh (p. 15)
invariance thought experiment (f/10+20 vs -f) to specify what the uncertainty must measure (p. 8)
property-list justification of an EI substitute without a Gaussian model (p. 15)
experiments: NOMAD 4, 18 default models vs no search, quad search, kriging, DFN, SHEBO; 7 analytical problems (15 instances, 1200(n+1)), aircraft range, simplified wing, solar1 (15 problem seeds, 10 replications), styrene; 4 NOMAD seeds (1 on solar1); data profiles at several τ, time data profiles, median table for SHEBO; losses to quad search on analytical problems and solar1 reported (pp. 16-28).
positioning: Frames BBO as direct search vs surrogate methods with the search-poll paradigm credited to Audet 2004; closest prior uses of model disagreement are multi-fidelity correlation works; builds on the OECV metric and Talgorn et al.'s SP1-SP8 (pp. 2-3, 11, 13).
writing: Design arguments by toy example before formulas (p. 8); concessions in result sentences (quad search 'must be favoured on cheap analytical problems', p. 19); a paragraph on what counts as a fair comparison (pp. 20-22).
limits_future: Models must stay cheap; no gain on analytical problems; quadratics better on solar1; future: decouple objective/constraint uncertainty types, other weights, simplex/PSS size, adaptive λ, local α, understanding formulations 'chosen on a purely empirical basis' (pp. 28-29).

method_links.note: All ensemble and Bayesian machinery lives in the Search, candidates projected on the mesh, Poll unchanged, convergence inherited.
Budgets in (n+1) units, data and time data profiles, seeds, other-family solvers, competitor's home ground conceded; variant: formulations and λ selected on the comparison problems.
solar1 (seed/replication parameters) and styrene from bbopt plus two MDO problems.
Constraint uncertainty built on sign/feasibility, not trend; for SHEBO violated constraints recast as hidden constraints.
Built on NOMAD 4 and its default model library.

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Kriging tested with its own best formulation SP5 rather than inside the formulations tuned for ensembles.

For a solver that cannot follow the common protocol, report median best value, time and evaluations to reach it, plus total time (pp. 26-28).
When replacing a Gaussian quantity by a non-probabilistic substitute, list the original's qualitative properties and keep them (p. 15).

The resulting algorithm benefits from the convergence results of MADS since all the candidate points lie on the mesh

title: Tight bounds on the maximal perimeter of convex equilateral small polygons
contribution: Constructs, for n = 2^s with s ≥ 4, convex equilateral small n-gons A_n whose perimeter is within π⁴/n⁴ + O(1/n⁵) of the upper bound and exceeds Mossinghoff's by 2π⁴/n⁴ + O(1/n⁵), proving Mossinghoff's hexadecagon suboptimal, and shows A_32 and A_64 are themselves not optimal.
problem_entry: Open extremal problem (n = 2^s, s ≥ 4) entered by beating the best known construction (Mossinghoff 2008) in the constant of the O(1/n⁴) gap (pp. 1-2).
key_idea: Define the polygon by its diameter graph (symmetry axis, half-path, pendant edges) so coordinates are closed-form in one angle t and equilaterality is one scalar equation; expand the root asymptotically (pp. 5-6).
assumptions: Vertices in upper half-plane, counterclockwise, v0 at origin; convexity by determinants σ_i ≥ 0; n = 2^s, s ≥ 4 only (pp. 2, 5).
proof_devices: diameter-graph-parameterized construction reducing the polygon to one angle (pp. 5-6)
asymptotic expansion of the root t0(n) (derivation not shown) (p. 6)
smallness and convexity checked by expanding critical distance and determinant (p. 6)
better instances Z32, Z64 from other diameter graphs as self-audit (Props. 1-2, pp. 7-8)
experiments: none (numerical table of perimeters for n = 16-256 and fraction of gap closed tending to 2/3, Table 1, p. 7)
positioning: Historical chain Reinhardt 1922, Vincze 1950, Datta 1997, Tamvakis 1987, Audet-Hansen-Messine(-Perron) 2004/2007, Mossinghoff 2008, Bingane 2021-22; improves directly on Mossinghoff's family (pp. 1-4).
writing: Main theorem stated on p. 2 before any construction; a single computational proof section; table with gap fraction (pp. 2, 5-7).
limits_future: Another family might improve Theorem 1; exact optima for s ≥ 4 remain out of reach (pp. 2, 8).

method_links.note: Rigor as a bound sandwich (upper bound, constructive lower bound, explicit gap constant) rather than a convergence ladder; self-audit shows own family suboptimal for n = 32, 64.
Released artifact is the OPTIGON code package (Julia/MATLAB vertex coordinates), not a blackbox benchmark.
The extremal-polygon line dated 2002-2013 in SKILL.md continues in 2022 with Bingane.

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Candidate extremal polygon encoded by a diameter graph plus symmetry, reducing to one scalar equation, then asymptotic expansion.

transferable: Report a new bound with the fraction of the remaining gap it closes and its limit as n grows (p. 7).
After an asymptotic result, test optimality at small n by exhibiting better instances (pp. 7-8).

quotes.text: In particular, for the first open case n = 16, our result proves that Mossinghoff’s equilateral hexadecagon is suboptimal.
This suggests that it is possible that another family of convex equilateral small polygons might produce an improvement to Theorem 1.

title: The equilateral small octagon of maximal width
contribution: Determines the equilateral small octagon of maximal width (w*₈ = 0.9537763006… + ε, 0 ≤ ε ≤ 10⁻⁶, ε-unique with radius 1.5×10⁻⁴) by combining analytic lemmas that leave two height-graph configurations with Couenne global-optimization certificates, and gives an asymptotic family G_n within 2π⁴/(3n⁴) + O(1/n⁶) of the width bound for n = 2^s, s ≥ 4.
problem_entry: First open case (n = 8) of the maximal width of equilateral small 2^s-gons, plus an asymptotic family for larger n (p. 1).
key_idea: Guess a height graph giving a candidate F8 in closed form, prune the space analytically (side-length bounds from the width-perimeter inequality, furthest-vertex lemmas, Ptolemy) to two configurations, then certify each with a global MINLP solver (pp. 5-9).
assumptions: Coordinates normalized (v0 at origin, upper half-plane, counterclockwise); certificate relies on Couenne's numerical tolerances, stated as ε ≤ 10⁻⁶ in the theorem (pp. 1, 4, 9).
proof_devices: contradiction by distance: two disjoint long diagonals force a distance > 1.0263 (Lemma 2, p. 7)
case reduction of height graphs to two configurations (Corollary 1, p. 7)
Ptolemy's inequality to tighten side-length and width bounds (Prop. 3, pp. 7-8)
global-solver certificates: infeasible configuration, raised objective bound infeasible (pp. 8-9)
ε-uniqueness via an exclusion-ball constraint made infeasible (Prop. 5, p. 9)
asymptotic expansion for the family G_n (pp. 10-11)
experiments: Solver runs as proof steps (Couenne via AMPL/NEOS: 0.32 s, 3.18 s, 2.05 s, 2.80 s) and a width table for n = 16-256 (pp. 9, 11).
positioning: Relative to Bezdek-Fodor 2000 (width theory), Audet-Hansen-Messine-Ninin 2013 (non-equilateral octagon), Audet-Hansen-Messine 2009 inequality and Bingane's lower bounds (pp. 1-4, 6).
writing: Both main results stated as Theorems 1-2 on pp. 1-2; lemma chain with short proofs; solver times given inside proofs (pp. 1-2, 7-9).
limits_future: Precision 10⁻⁶ and uniqueness only outside a 1.5×10⁻⁴ ball; Theorem 1's 'only attained' is stronger than the ε-uniqueness proved; no future work stated (pp. 1, 9, 11).

method_links.note: Tolerance written into the theorem and claim fenced by an explicit certificate; device is case reduction plus global solver, not counterexamples.
AMPL models released so the certificate can be rerun.
The PhD-era global-optimization toolkit is still used in 2022, now via an off-the-shelf solver.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: analytic pruning before a global-solver certificate
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Variable bounds and configuration elimination by hand until each remaining MINLP closes in seconds.
Adding ||z - z*||² ≥ 2.25×10⁻⁸ makes the model infeasible, proving near-uniqueness.

transferable: Write the solver tolerance into the theorem statement (value + ε, 0 ≤ ε ≤ 10⁻⁶) (p. 1).
Use a known inequality between two functionals plus the best known value of one to bound the variables of the other problem (p. 6).
Certify optimality by raising the objective's lower bound slightly and showing infeasibility (p. 9).

quotes.text: This paper solves the first open case and finds the optimal equilateral small octagon.
Within the limit of the numerical computations, this corresponds to the octagon F8.

title: A general mathematical framework for constrained mixed-variable blackbox optimization problems with meta and categorical variables
contribution: Introduces a notation framework for mixed-variable blackbox problems in which meta variables decree which variables and constraints are acting, separates nominal/ordinal categorical from integer/continuous variables, defines the domain and feasible set via meta-parameterized sets, and casts direct search (subproblems plus user-defined neighborhoods) and Bayesian optimization (auxiliary problem with encoders and mixed kernels) in it; no experiments.
problem_entry: Meta variables (switching other variables and constraints on or off) and metric-free categorical variables make mixed-variable BBO hard, and earlier frameworks conflated categorical with integer and meta with categorical variables (pp. 2-3, 10).
key_idea: Partition x = (x^m, x^q, x^s) with types and roles (meta, decreed, global), parameterize sets by the meta component, and express solution strategies as standard subproblems or an auxiliary problem (pp. 7-27).
assumptions: No meta variable decreed by another meta variable; meta variables not encoded for BO; noise-free zero-mean GP; constraints handled inside subproblem solvers (pp. 8, 23-25).
proof_devices: none: definitions only (Defs. 1-9); no theorems or convergence statement (pp. 7-25)
experiments: none (stated, with the surrogate management framework as precedent, p. 2)
positioning: Builds on Audet-Dennis mixed-variable GPS lineage and 'importantly relies' on Lucidi-Piccialli(-Sciandrone) dimensional variables, which it generalizes and renames; critiques relax-and-round one-hot BO; reviews GP categorical kernels and Pelamatti et al. (pp. 2-4, 8).
writing: Definitions interleaved with one running MLP hyperparameter example; each modelling choice justified right after it (integer vs categorical split p. 10, renaming p. 8); arXiv v1 has broken cross-references (pp. 18, 23, 28).
limits_future: No experiments and no theory; future computational studies and BO development bridging optimization and machine learning (pp. 2, 28).

method_links.note: Classify-before-solving applied to variables: type and role for every variable, global vs decreed for every constraint, decision tree; axis is switching, not relaxability.
Architecture only: flexible global search before a poll over user-defined neighborhoods, a poll alone misses good points; no convergence claimed.
The 'Hallé-Hannan → categorical framework 2023' entry; MSc scholarships acknowledged.

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Vocabulary published first, no experiments, justified by the SMF precedent; algorithms (CatMADS) follow later per SKILL.md.
'dimensional' renamed 'meta' because it clashes with physical units in engineering.

transferable: Thread one small realistic example through every definition and end with the fully instantiated sets and constraints (pp. 5-6, 16-18).
Define neighborhoods of metric-free variables as sets of rules that may depend on the whole point, writing boundary cases explicitly (p. 21).
In a mixed-kernel GP, compare conditional components only when the switching components are equal (p. 27).

quotes.text: The decree property is a special property that only meta variables possess.
By its own, a poll is prone to miss out good point solutions.

title: Sequential stochastic blackbox optimization with zeroth-order gradient estimators
contribution: Proposes SSO, which solves a sequence of Gaussian-smoothed problems with decreasing smoothing β_i by a zeroth-order Signum whose vanishing momentum step reduces variance and whose momentum norm is the stopping test; proves expectation rates for ZO-Signum under Lipschitz F and an evaluation complexity for SSO under smoothness and local convexity; competitive on SOLAR and blackbox adversarial attacks.
problem_entry: Gap in prior work [43]: smoothing's convexification with large β was used without β → 0, with fixed inner iterations, without convergence proof or rate, on analytical problems only (pp. 2-3).
key_idea: Homotopy in the smoothing parameter: β_i = β0/(i+1)² defines both the subproblem and its tolerance ||m|| ≤ Lβ_i/(4β0); ZO-Signum with decaying momentum step; optional MADS-style finite search step before the convergent local step (pp. 5-8).
assumptions: F(·,ξ) integrable and L0-Lipschitz, no differentiability (Assumption 1); for SSO rates also Lipschitz gradient (Assumption 2) and local convexity of f^{β_i} with starts inside the convex ball for i ≥ I (Assumption 3) (pp. 4, 18-19).
proof_devices: descent + bias + variance decomposition following Bernstein et al. (Prop. 4.1, p. 9)
cross term vanishes by conditioning on the σ-field and unbiasedness (Lemma 4.2, pp. 9-10)
E||g̃||² ≤ L0²(n+4)² via Nesterov-Spokoiny moment bound (Lemma 4.3, p. 10)
split-sum bound on the decaying-momentum weights (Lemma 4.4, pp. 10-11)
random output iterate R uniform in [C, K] for the expectation rate (Theorem 4.9, p. 14)
small momentum implies small gradient under local convexity, summed over subproblems for the complexity (Lemma 4.13, Theorem 4.17, pp. 19-23)
experiments: SOLAR instance 2 as a feasibility problem (integers fixed), 1000 evaluations, mean of 5 seeds vs NOMAD 3.9.1, CMA-ES, ZO-adaMM; adversarial attacks on Cifar10 (100 images, 5000 queries) and ImageNet with success rate, distortion and evaluations; per-problem hyperparameters outside the analysed step exponents (pp. 24-26, 30).
positioning: Related work split into stochastic direct search/model-based vs ZO gradient methods; [43] singled out as the last work to exploit convexification; rates compared with ZO-SGD, ZO-signSGD, ZO-adaMM, ZSCG in a table that shows ZO-Signum worse (pp. 2-3, 17-18).
writing: Three contribution bullets (pp. 3-4); workflow tables of lemmas/theorems (pp. 8, 18); explicit statement of worse rates (p. 17); 'first of its kind' hedged with 'to the best of our knowledge' (pp. 23, 27).
limits_future: Stronger dimension dependence, sign loses gradient magnitude, fixed term large if the convex region is hard to reach; future: constrained stochastic problems (pp. 15, 17, 23, 27).

method_links.note: Contradicts SKILL.md's claim that complexity-style guarantees are absent from Audet's corpus and the Roundtable remark that no Audet abstract gives expected bounds: expectation rates and an evaluation complexity are proved; ladder shape (Lipschitz → convex → smooth + locally convex) is evidence, no counterexamples.
Search/local split exported to a stochastic gradient method; finite search budget so convergence rests on the local step; no mesh.
SOLAR reused from bbopt.
Other-family baselines (NOMAD, CMA-ES) but mean-of-5-seeds curves only, per-problem tuned hyperparameters, no data profiles.
NOMAD excluded from adversarial attacks because it 'is not recommended for large problems'.
